newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges higher, Aug/Oct prevails.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges higher, Aug/Oct prevails.

text.p: The nearby August/October spread dominated trading on London's white sugar futures market on Monday but price movements were still tight across the board.
Although the two front and other months saw some flat-price buying and crossed trades earlier in the session, the spread accounted for most of the turnover.
"The interest is in the spread...but they've lost their interest now. It's certainly died down a little this afternoon," said one trader.
"You're probably talking a little bit of physical offtake if the spread is moving a touch," he said.
A mixed bag of players was reported to be behind the day's activity but French brokers were prominent.
The spot August contract was little changed from the morning and at 1540 GMT stood 90 cents higher at $310.10, down from its Friday's peak of $312.50 which will now act as nearby resistance.
October was down 10 cents at $304.60 and other months were slightly firmer. Volume totalled 1,111 lots.
Traders said there was little interest in the August/July arbitrage, which was trading at around $66, and said some selling would only appear if the premium widened further.
But the fact that July raws was holding above 11.00 cents/lb was encouraging, they said.
The Paris market was still very quiet with only 37 lots of spot August posted on the board. The position was down 20 cents at $309.80.
